text: SPECTRA (Sparse-Precision Exact Channel Tensor Reconstruction Architecture) is an architecture-agnostic neural compression engine and high-throughput execution runtime engineered to break the Memory Wall on consumer and edge GPUs (including 4 GB and 8 GB NVIDIA RTX laptop and desktop GPUs). Run mathematical reasoning models (such as DeepSeek-R1-Distill ), deep transformers ( IBM Granite-3B , Llama-3.2 ), state-space hybrids ( NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Nano Mamba-2 ), and convolutional architectures ( LiquidAI LFM-3 ) locally on hardware where standard runtimes crash with Out-of-Memory (OOM) errors. Tip Running modern large language models (LLMs) and hybrid state-space models (SSMs) on edge and consumer devices is fundamentally bounded by memory bandwidth rather than arithmetic throughput. During single-token autoregressive generation ( $M = 1$ ), an inference engine must read the entire weight matrix $W$ from GPU global memory (GDDR6/VRAM) to evaluate a single token vector $x$ : $$\text{Operational Arithmetic Intensity} \approx \frac{2 \cdot N \cdot K \text{ FLOPs}}{2 \cdot N \cdot K \text{ Bytes loaded}} = 1.0\text{ FLOP/Byte}$$ On a consumer GPU such as the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Ti Laptop GPU: To accelerate decoding, the weight bytes transferred across the memory bus must be compressed. However, traditional quantization tools introduce severe friction: SPECTRA eliminates all three barriers through mathematical guarantees. SPECTRA requires zero manual setup. Cloning & Serving Pre-Tuned Models Cloning any pre-compressed SPECTRA model directly into your workspace makes it immediately runnable: # Example A: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-1.5B (Reasoning model, 1.03 GB) git clone https://huggingface.co/neuracryption/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-1.5B-SPECTRA # Example B: NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Nano-4B (Mamba-2 Hybrid, 2.26 GB) git clone https://huggingface.co/neuracryption/Nemotron-3-Nano-4B-SPECTRA # Example C: IBM Granite-4.2-3B (Deep 40-layer Transformer, 2.06 GB) git clone https://huggingface.co/neuracryption/Granite-4.2-3B-SPECTRA # Example D: LiquidAI LFM-3-1.7B (Hybrid ConvNet/SSM, 1.00 GB) git clone https://huggingface.co/neuracryption/LFM-3-1.7B-SPECTRA Step 2: Run Immediate CLI Inference python run_inference.py --prompt " Explain quantum computing in simple terms: " Step 3: Or Open the Web Dashboard python launch.py The scanner automatically registers all cloned models and populates the Ready-to-Run grid. SPECTRA is 100% architecturally agnostic . You can compress any model from the Hugging Face Hub or local disk without modifying code: # Compress directly via CLI: spectra compress \ --model meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct \ --output ./models/llama3_spectra.trdc \ --group-size 32 \ --outliers 0.01 Or compress within Python: from spectra import Spectra Spectra . compress ( model_id_or_path = "mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1" , output_path = "models/mistral7b.trdc" ) Why Compression Never Crashes Your Machine: Zero-RAM Shard Streaming: Reads safetensors or bin shards tensor-by-tensor from disk. Host RAM stays strictly under 50 MB. Mathematical Matrix Classification: Any 2D weight matrix with dimension divisible by 32 (Attention Q/K/V/O, MLP gate/up/down, MoE routed experts, Mamba projections) is compressed to 4-bit Group-32 + HDSQ outlier channels. Lossless Structural Vectors: RMSNorm, LayerNorm, biases, 1D convolution filters, and RoPE tables are preserved losslessly in native FP16/BF16 precision. Calibration-Free Group-32 Microscaling Rather than calculating global or per-channel scales that can be distorted by heavy-tailed outliers, SPECTRA partitions weights into blocks of 32 contiguous parameters: $$W_{\text{quant}} = \text{clamp}\left(\left\lfloor \frac{W - \min(W)}{\text{Scale}} \right\rceil, 0, 15\right)$$ In neural architectures with LayerNorm or RMSNorm preceding linear projections: $$y = W \cdot \text{RMSNorm}(x) = W \cdot \left(\frac{x}{\text{RMS}(x)} \odot \gamma\right)$$ The learned affine scale vector $\gamma$ analytically mirrors the parameter Hessian curvature: $$F_{jj} \propto |\gamma_j|^2$$ SPECTRA inspects the model Abstract Syntax Tree (AST), pairs every linear layer with its upstream normalization vector, and computes column saliency: $$S_j = |\gamma_j| \cdot |W_{:,j}|_2$$ This computation takes under 50 milliseconds across an entire 7B model and requires zero calibration data.
